newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scorpions kill six near Algerian desert town.
newsitem.headline: Scorpions kill six near Algerian desert town.

text.p: Scorpions stung 1,462 people, killing six of them, in and around the Saharan town of Ouargla in Algeria in the first half of this year, local officials said on Tuesday.
The officials, quoted by the Algerian news agency APS, said around half of those poisoned by scorpions were stricken in the town area, with the rest in outlying areas of the province.
Algeria's main oil field Hassi Messaoud, where a number of foreigners work, had the least number of stings in the province, a total of 27.
For the whole of last year, 11 people died in Ouargla province from scorpion stings. Throughout Algeria, around 30,000 people are stung each year and more than 100 die, APS said.
